about: Prerequisite graph for a German grammar trainer. 'requires' edges are hard prerequisites; 'sequence' is one valid study order (topological, level-first).

WO.name: Word order
WO.why: German word order is acquired in a fixed sequence (Pienemann's stages). Teaching a stage before the previous one is stable doesn't stick, so this track's order is not negotiable.

CASE.name: Case and the noun phrase
CASE.why: L2 learners move from one case, to nominative vs. 'other', to a full three-case system. Accusative and dative must be separated before Rektion can work.

VERB.name: Verb forms and tenses
VERB.why: Forms the other tracks lean on: Konjunktiv II needs Präteritum stems, passive needs participles, double infinitives need modals in Perfekt.

REK.name: Rektion (valency)
REK.why: Which preposition and case a verb, adjective or noun takes, and what the pair means. TW's diagnosed gap; Kasusschloss already covers REK2 and part of REK3.

MOOD.name: Mood: Konjunktiv II and I
MOOD.why: Hypotheticals, politeness, counterfactuals, reported speech. TW's other diagnosed gap.

CL.name: Clauses and connectors
CL.why: Joining clauses, and knowing what each connector does to word order.

ST.name: Style and register (C-level)
ST.why: What separates C1/C2 from B2: compression, nominal style, particles, inferential modals.

drill_types.SORT: Categorize under time pressure (like Case sprint). Best for: which bin does this belong in?
drill_types.MEANING: Multiple choice with near-miss distractors, both directions (like Bedeutung). Best for: what does this mean / which form means this?
drill_types.PRODUCE: Type the form from a cue (article, ending, verb form). Exact-match grading.
drill_types.CLOZE: Sentence with one gap; type the missing word (like Sentence card). Feedback shows typed → correct → rule.
drill_types.ORDER: Tap shuffled sentence chunks into the right order. The only drill that directly trains word order.
drill_types.TRANSFORM: Rewrite a sentence (active→passive, weil→wegen, direct→reported speech). Grade against a small set of accepted answers.

mastery.working: accuracy >= 85% over the last 20 attempts. Enough to unlock dependents.
mastery.fluent: accuracy >= 95% AND at or above the unit's rate aim in a 1-minute sprint.
mastery.retained: still fluent on a check at least 3 days after reaching fluent. Only retained units drop to maintenance review.

learner.placement: Roughly A2/B1 (Goethe 'Test your German' 16/30). Treat A1 units and most A2 units as probably known: verify with a short placement probe per unit instead of teaching from scratch.

units.title: Verb second in main clauses
units.scope: Subject first, finite verb in position 2. Statements and W-questions; yes/no questions verb-first.

units.title: Coordinating conjunctions keep main-clause order
units.scope: und, aber, oder, denn, sondern sit in 'position 0' and change nothing.
units.english_trap: denn means because but behaves like und, not like weil.

units.title: Present tense
units.scope: Regular endings, sein/haben, stem-changing verbs (fahren → fährt, sehen → sieht).

units.title: Modal verbs
units.scope: können, müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen, mögen/möchten; no -t in er/sie/es.
units.english_trap: muss nicht = don't have to; darf nicht = must not.

units.title: Separable and inseparable prefixes
units.scope: an-, auf-, aus-, ein-, mit-, zu- split off; be-, er-, ver-, zer-, ge-, emp-, ent-, miss- never do.

units.title: The sentence bracket (Satzklammer)
units.scope: Modal + infinitive at the end; separable prefix at the end. Pienemann's stage 'verb separation'.
units.english_trap: English keeps verb parts together: 'I must today work' feels wrong but is the German shape.

units.title: Gender, nominative and plurals
units.scope: der/die/das, ein/eine, kein; the main plural patterns.

units.title: Accusative: direct objects
units.scope: Only masculine changes (den/einen); pronouns mich, dich, ihn, uns, euch, sie.

units.title: Imperative
units.scope: du/ihr/Sie forms, including sei and stem changes (lies!, gib!).

units.title: Inversion after a fronted element
units.scope: Anything in position 1 (Heute, Dann, Im Sommer) pushes the subject after the verb. Acquired after the bracket.
units.english_trap: 'Today I go' → Heute gehe ich, never Heute ich gehe.

units.title: Verb last in subordinate clauses
units.scope: weil/dass/wenn/ob clauses send the finite verb to the end. The last of Pienemann's core stages.

units.title: Dative: indirect objects and dative verbs
units.scope: dem/der/dem/den+n; mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen; helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören, gratulieren take dative.
units.english_trap: 'help him' is ihm helfen, not ihn.

units.title: The 14-preposition case lock
units.scope: Always Akk: für um gegen über (in Rektion). Always Dat: aus von mit zu nach vor unter. Switchers: an auf in.

units.title: Two-way prepositions in space: wo? vs. wohin?
units.scope: Location → Dativ, direction → Akkusativ; the verb pairs liegen/legen, stehen/stellen, sitzen/setzen, hängen.

units.title: Possessives and kein
units.scope: mein/dein/sein/ihr/unser/euer/ihr take ein-word endings in all cases.

units.title: Perfekt
units.scope: haben vs. sein (movement/change of state); regular and irregular participles; no ge- with -ieren or inseparable prefixes.

units.title: Reflexive verbs
units.scope: Accusative reflexive (ich wasche mich) vs. dative when there is another object (ich wasche mir die Hände).

units.title: Verb valency: who gets the dative, who gets the accusative
units.scope: geben, schenken, zeigen, erklären: jemandem (Dat) etwas (Akk).

units.title: Polite chunks
units.scope: Ich hätte gern..., Ich möchte..., Könnten Sie...?, Würden Sie...? Memorized as phrases before the system.

units.title: Core subordinators
units.scope: weil, dass, wenn, ob, als; als (once, past) vs. wenn (whenever / if).
units.english_trap: 'when' in the past (one time) is als, not wenn.

units.title: Subordinate clause first: verb, comma, verb
units.scope: Weil es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. The whole clause counts as position 1.

units.title: Middle-field order and nicht
units.scope: Pronoun before noun; dative noun before accusative noun; accusative pronoun before dative pronoun; time-cause-manner-place; where nicht goes.

units.title: Adjective endings
units.scope: Three patterns: after der-words (weak), after ein-words (mixed), with no article (strong). Teach as 'the ending shows the case if the article didn't'.

units.title: Genitive
units.scope: des/der, -s/-es on the noun; wegen, trotz, während, statt; spoken German often swaps in von + Dat.

units.title: n-declension nouns
units.scope: Herr, Kollege, Student, Mensch take -n/-en outside the nominative singular.

units.title: Future and werden
units.scope: werden + infinitive for future and for 'probably'; the three jobs of werden (become, future, passive).

units.title: Passive, present and past
units.scope: wird gemacht, wurde gemacht; von + Dat for the agent. Then (B2) passive with modals, Perfekt passive (ist gemacht worden), Zustandspassiv (ist geschlossen).

units.title: Präteritum, including strong-verb stems
units.scope: war/hatte/modals first, then the strong stems (kam, gab, ging, wusste, brachte). Konjunktiv II is built from these.

units.title: Plusquamperfekt
units.scope: hatte/war + participle; the 'before the past' tense nachdem demands.

units.title: Core verb + preposition pairs, fixed-case prepositions
units.scope: Meaning, preposition and case for ~45 core pairs (warten auf, halten von, Angst haben vor...).
units.english_trap: English prepositions mislead: wait FOR = warten AUF.

units.title: Switcher pairs: an/auf/in + Akk vs. Dat per verb
units.scope: denken an + Akk but teilnehmen an + Dat; bestehen auf + Dat. The ~15 that must be memorized one by one.

units.title: Question words and pronouns: worauf? / auf wen?
units.scope: Things take wo(r)- and da(r)-: Worauf wartest du? Ich warte darauf. People take preposition + pronoun: Auf wen? Auf ihn.

units.title: zu-infinitives: um...zu, ohne...zu, statt...zu
units.scope: Es ist schwer, Deutsch zu lernen; um...zu vs. damit (same vs. different subject).

units.title: da-compound + clause
units.scope: Ich freue mich darauf, dass du kommst / dich zu sehen. The da-word points ahead to the clause.
units.english_trap: 'I look forward to seeing you' has no -ing in German.

units.title: Konjunktiv II present: würde + infinitive, wäre, hätte
units.scope: Wishes and unreal conditions: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich kommen. Ich wünschte, ich wäre...
units.english_trap: 'If I would have' is not German: the wenn-clause takes hätte, not würde... haben.

units.title: Konjunktiv II of modals: advice and possibility
units.scope: könnte (could), müsste (ought to/should probably), sollte (should), dürfte (probably).

units.title: Relative clauses (Nom, Akk, Dat)
units.scope: der/den/dem/die/denen; gender from the noun, case from the role in the relative clause.

units.title: Time clauses and tense sequence
units.scope: bevor, nachdem (+ Plusquamperfekt), während, seit(dem), bis, sobald.

units.title: Double infinitive and the Ersatzinfinitiv
units.scope: Ich habe kommen müssen; in a subordinate clause the finite verb jumps in front: dass ich habe kommen müssen.

units.title: lassen and participles as adjectives
units.scope: Ich lasse das Auto reparieren; der schlafende Hund, die geschlossene Tür.

units.title: Adjective + preposition
units.scope: stolz auf, abhängig von, interessiert an, zufrieden mit, verantwortlich für, bekannt für.

units.title: Noun + preposition
units.scope: Angst vor, Interesse an, Lust auf, Hoffnung auf, Grund für, Kritik an. Usually mirrors the verb.

units.title: Konjunktiv II past: counterfactuals
units.scope: Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen. hätte/wäre + participle, haben/sein choice as in Perfekt.

units.title: Synthetic Konjunktiv II of strong verbs
units.scope: käme, gäbe, ginge, wüsste, bräuchte, ließe. Built from the Präteritum stem plus umlaut.

units.title: Modal double infinitive in Konjunktiv II
units.scope: Du hättest anrufen sollen. Wenn ich hätte kommen können, ... The hardest structure in TW's diagnostic.
units.english_trap: 'should have called' → hättest anrufen sollen, never hättest angerufen gesollt.

units.title: als ob / als + Konjunktiv II
units.scope: Er tut, als ob er nichts wüsste / als wüsste er nichts (verb right after als).

units.title: Connector types by word order
units.scope: Sort every connector: position 0 (aber, denn), adverb with inversion (deshalb, trotzdem, außerdem), subordinator with verb-final (obwohl, da). Perfect for a SORT sprint.
units.english_trap: trotzdem and obwohl mean nearly the same but take opposite word order.

units.title: Two-part connectors
units.scope: entweder...oder, weder...noch, sowohl...als auch, nicht nur...sondern auch, je...desto (verb-final, then inversion).

units.title: Relative clauses with genitive and prepositions
units.scope: dessen/deren; mit dem, über die; wo(r)- after etwas, alles, das.

units.title: Nominal style ↔ verbal style
units.scope: weil er krank war ↔ wegen seiner Krankheit; nachdem er angekommen war ↔ nach seiner Ankunft.

units.title: Noun-verb combinations (Funktionsverbgefüge)
units.scope: in Frage kommen, zur Verfügung stellen, Abschied nehmen von, eine Entscheidung treffen, Kritik üben an.

units.title: Extended Rektion inventory
units.scope: Grow from the core set to ~200 pairs, ordered by corpus frequency (DWDS).

units.title: Konjunktiv I: reported speech
units.scope: er sei, er habe, er komme; switch to Konjunktiv II where Konjunktiv I looks like the indicative (sie haben → sie hätten).

units.title: Conditionals without wenn
units.scope: Hätte ich das gewusst, wäre ich gekommen. Sollten Sie Fragen haben, ...

units.title: Extended participial attributes
units.scope: die von der Regierung gestern beschlossene Reform. Read right to left from the noun.

units.title: Modal particles
units.scope: doch, ja, mal, eben, halt, wohl, schon, eigentlich: what each does to tone. Meaning-in-context, not translation.
units.english_trap: Most have no English word; drill the effect, not a gloss.

units.title: Subjective modals
units.scope: Er soll reich sein (reportedly); er will es gesehen haben (claims); das dürfte stimmen; das müsste klappen.

units.title: Register and idiom
units.scope: Shift a text between spoken, neutral and written-formal; fixed idioms. Largely outside drill territory: pair with reading and Diktat.
